title: Dialog
description: A dialog (#618): who speaks it, always a person (monsters never talk), and the lines they say, read in the file's order. A line can offer the player answers instead of reading on: each ends the dialog, or leads to the line it names. Choosing an answer raises an event naming the dialog's id and the answer's id, which quests count and branch on (#573, #624), so neither id is ever reused or changed once shipped. One file per dialog, named after its id.

id.description: Stable, never reused: lowercase words joined by underscores.

speaker.description: The player-facing name of who says the lines.

speaker_codex.description: The speaker's codex entry (#959): what the player reads on their codex page. People have no content file of their own, so it rides on the dialog they speak.

entry.description: A short text about them and where their name comes from.

gloss.description: What their name means, hand-written (#959), e.g. "Teska, sworn to the guild".

lock.description: Whether the dialog holds its player until they finish it (#891): only for rare story beats and scripted events, never an average quest giver. Every dialog states it.

lines.description: The lines, in the order they're read where no answer leads elsewhere; the dialog ends after the last.

id.description: Its id within the dialog, which answers name to lead to it; needed only there, and unique.

answers.description: The answers the player chooses from; left out, the dialog reads on to the next line.

id.description: Unique within the dialog, never reused: what quests name the answer by.

next.description: The id of the line it leads to; left out, the dialog ends with it.

commits.description: Whether choosing it has effects (#891), like a step a quest counts: from it on, the dialog holds its player until they finish it. An answer with effects must be marked; left out, it has none.
